at least one grill here brushes satay sauce on everything. Satay and I have history, so that stall is crossed out.

venue_assessment.night_market_hollow_oak: Out: peanuts everywhere (peanut butter, peanut sauce, peanut slaw).
venue_assessment.campus_bun_stop: $, peanut-free, black bean patty works for Mina, but butter-toasted brioche, cheese on classics and garlic-butter fries hit Roxy's dairy intolerance: 2 stars.
venue_assessment.night_market_amber_lamp: $, peanut-free (checked jar by jar), black bean and mushroom meatless burgers that are also animal-free, oil not butter, no cheese: 3 stars.
venue_assessment.night_market_velvet_tent: Out: board is all meat, nothing for Mina.
venue_assessment.night_market_midnight_orchard: $$ (one tier over), otherwise peanut-free, vegan-friendly, dairy-free: 2 stars.
venue_assessment.night_market_crooked_pine: Out: $$$, two tiers over Maya's budget.

notes: Peanut allergy is signalled indirectly ('Satay and I have history'); Liam's 'peanut-y' line confirms it, so it is fair.
Mina's diet is never named outright. 'Zero meat' reads as vegetarian; the lunch-on-fries story hints at something stricter. Amber Lamp works either way, so the ambiguity does not change the answer.
Roxy's dairy intolerance is clear from 'hold the cheese, no creamy sauce, no shake' plus the milkshake incident reference.
Bun Stop is a solid decoy (cheap, peanut-free, vegan patty) and the only thing against it is dairy, which is buried in the first review. Good trap.

Possible inconsistency: Liam says that at campus burger night 'nothing else on the menu worked' for Mina, yet the Bun Stop review says its black bean patty is 'from the campus days' and is 'still on the board'. If Bun Stop is the campus counter Liam means, the story contradicts the review. If it is a different campus burger night, a player may still be confused.
Maya's budget line is clear: 'a little over' = -1 star, 'fancy' = deal-breaker, which matches the tiers.
